test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following devices does NOT use the heating effect of current for its working?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Mixer Grinder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **heating effect of electric current**, also known as **Joule heating**, occurs when an electric current passes through a conductor with **resistance**, leading to the production of **heat energy**.
 
• **Electric Mixer Grinder**: This device primarily works on the **magnetic effect of electric current**. It contains an **electric motor** that converts **electrical energy** into **mechanical energy** to rotate the blades. While it may get warm due to friction and internal resistance, its primary working principle is not the heating effect. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Electric Iron**: This appliance uses a **heating element** made of high-resistance material like **Nichrome**. When current flows through it, the resistance converts the **electrical energy** into **heat**, which is then used to press clothes. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Electric Geyser**: It functions by passing current through an **immersion rod** or a heating coil. The high **resistance** of the coil generates significant **thermal energy**, which is transferred to the **water** to increase its **temperature**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **Electric Fuse**: A **fuse** is a critical safety device designed to protect circuits. It consists of a **wire** with a **low melting point**. When **excessive current** flows, the **heating effect** causes the wire to **melt** and break the **circuit**. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Joule’s Law of Heating**: The amount of heat produced (**H**) in a conductor is directly proportional to the **square of the current** (**I²**), the **resistance** (**R**) of the conductor, and the **time** (**t**) for which the current flows. The formula is expressed as **H = I²Rt**.
 
• **Magnetic Effect of Current**: Discovered by **Hans Christian Oersted** in **1820**, this principle states that a **current-carrying conductor** produces a **magnetic field** around it. This is the fundamental principle behind **electric motors**, **fans**, and **mixers**.
 
• **Nichrome**: It is an **alloy** consisting of **Nickel** and **Chromium**. It is widely used in heating appliances because of its **high resistivity** and high **melting point**, and because it does not **oxidize** (burn) easily at **high temperatures**.
 
• **Energy Transformation**: In heating devices, **electrical energy** is transformed into **heat energy**. In motorized devices like the **Mixer Grinder**, **electrical energy** is transformed into **kinetic energy** (mechanical energy).
 
• **Applications of Heating Effect**: Apart from irons and geysers, other examples include **electric toasters**, **electric kettles**, **room heaters**, and **hair dryers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resistance Factor**: The **efficiency** of a heating device depends on the **material** used. For example, **Copper** has low resistance and is used for **connecting wires** to prevent heat loss, while **Tungsten** is used in **bulbs** because it can withstand **temperatures** up to **3422 degrees Celsius** while emitting **light**.
 
• **Fuse Characteristics**: A **fuse wire** is typically made of an **alloy of tin and lead**. It must have **high resistance** (to heat up quickly) and a **low melting point** (to break the circuit promptly during a **short circuit** or **overload**).
 
• **Safety in Appliances**: Modern homes often use **MCBs (Miniature Circuit Breakers)** instead of traditional fuses. While fuses work on the **heating effect**, **MCBs** often utilize the **magnetic effect** to trip the switch during **faults**.
